artifacts.name: Drover's Penny
artifacts.blurb: A copper penny worn smooth on one side by a thumb.
artifacts.inscription: Scratched on the worn side: a little tree, green all year.

artifacts.name: Silver Sixpence
artifacts.blurb: Bent once for luck, and straightened again.
artifacts.inscription: Pricked into the silver: a bowl, a dip in the land.

artifacts.name: Worn Guinea
artifacts.blurb: Gold, and older than anyone's grandmother.
artifacts.inscription: Stamped over the old king's head: a tiny six-pointed star.

artifacts.name: Lantern Frame
artifacts.blurb: Blackened iron, still square, still sound.
artifacts.inscription: Scratched in the soot: "Light it on the longest night."

artifacts.name: Lantern Glass
artifacts.blurb: A pane of wavy glass, wrapped in oilcloth and tucked out of the water.
artifacts.inscription: Painted on the glass in faded red: berries, and the words "not for eating".

artifacts.name: Lantern Wick
artifacts.blurb: A coil of wick in a tin that kept it dry for a hundred years.
artifacts.inscription: A label on the tin, in the founder's hand: "For the walk down into the hollow."

artifacts.name: Faded Blue Ribbon
artifacts.blurb: First Prize, Harvest Festival. The year is too faded to read.
artifacts.inscription: Embroidered on the tail: a sprig of holly and the word "Midwinter".

artifacts.name: Prize Rosette
artifacts.blurb: Red and gold silk folds: Best Basket in the Valley.
artifacts.inscription: Stitched on the back: "Under the tree that was old when the house was new."

artifacts.name: Judge's Medal
artifacts.blurb: A brass medal stamped with a chanterelle, given only once a generation.
artifacts.inscription: On the reverse: "When nothing else will fruit."

artifacts.name: Brass Compass Rose
artifacts.blurb: The needle still swings north, then thinks better of it and points down.
artifacts.inscription: Engraved round the rim: "Low ground, where the walls are."

artifacts.name: Sealed Map Tube
artifacts.blurb: Waxed shut. Inside, a chart of tunnels no one alive has walked.
artifacts.inscription: Inked on the chart: a churchyard tree, drawn where the walls stood.

artifacts.name: Surveyor's Chain
artifacts.blurb: A hundred iron links, each exactly as long as the last.
artifacts.inscription: A brass tag on the last link: "Measured from the Old Hearth: forty links."

artifacts.name: Stone Cap
artifacts.blurb: The cap of a mushroom carved in pale stone, broken clean at the stem.
artifacts.inscription: Carved under the cap: "I built the first house in the hollow, beside a tree older than the valley's name."

artifacts.name: Stone Stem
artifacts.blurb: A stone stem, broken at both ends, smooth from handling.
artifacts.inscription: Carved round the stem: "Dig when the ground is white."

artifacts.name: Stone Ring
artifacts.blurb: A carved ring that once sat under a stone cap.
artifacts.inscription: Carved inside the ring: a needled tree hung with red berries.

artifacts.name: Iron Door Key
artifacts.blurb: Heavy as a trowel, with the family mark on the bow.
artifacts.inscription: Filed into the bow, beside the family mark: a sprig of yew.

artifacts.name: Willow Basket Handle
artifacts.blurb: Plaited willow, dark with age and still supple.
artifacts.inscription: Woven in darker willow: "Gathered in winter, when the basket is empty."

artifacts.name: Hearth Tile
artifacts.blurb: A fired tile painted with a ring of little mushrooms.
artifacts.inscription: On the back, written before firing: "The house stood in the hollow. Look above it, not below."

sets.name: The Drover's Purse
sets.rule: Start every story year with 2 more coins.
sets.clue: Grandma said a drover once lost his purse on the way through the valley, a coin here and a coin there, and spent the rest of his life looking under the wrong trees.
sets.payoff: Penny, sixpence and guinea, together again. The drover's purse is whole: 2 more coins every year.

sets.name: The Forager's Lantern
sets.rule: Rare finds and artifacts glint through the leaves before you turn them.
sets.clue: Great-aunt Rue said the first forager in the family carried a lantern that could find a mushroom in the dark, and that it came apart in three places.
sets.payoff: Frame, glass and wick: the old lantern burns again. Rare finds glint before you turn them.

sets.name: The Festival Ribbons
sets.rule: 2 more festival points every story year: the judges remember the family.
sets.clue: Grandpa said the family once won every prize at the Harvest Festival, and hid the ribbons away when times got hard.
sets.payoff: Every old ribbon, found. The judges remember the family: 2 more festival points every year.

sets.name: The Mapmaker's Case
sets.rule: The way down lies in a zone's first deep patch, not its last.
sets.clue: Great-grandpa said a mapmaker charted every tunnel under the valley, then lost the pieces of his kit in three different holes.
sets.payoff: The mapmaker's case is whole, and his charts show the shortcuts: the way down lies in the first deep patch.

sets.name: The Mushroom Stones
sets.rule: A bust keeps one more of your finds.
sets.clue: Great-uncle Tobias said the old people carved a mushroom out of stone for luck, then broke it in three so no one could steal the luck.
sets.payoff: Cap, stem and ring: the lucky stone mushroom is whole again. A bust keeps one more find.

sets.name: The First Homestead
sets.rule: One more basket slot: the first homestead's basket, rewoven.
sets.clue: Grandpa said that one day someone in the family would find the way back to where it all began.
sets.payoff: Key, basket and hearth: the first homestead, remembered. Its basket, rewoven, holds one more find.

cache.name: The Founder's Cellar
cache.premise: Every heirloom the founder left is marked. Put the marks together and dig: the right spot, in the right place, at the right time of year.
cache.wrong: Roots and cold earth, and nothing else. The founder never dug here. The day is spent, so you head home.
cache.place: A hand's depth under the Yew, the spade rings on oak. A trapdoor, and under it a cellar no bigger than a larder, dry as the day it was dug. Empty jars on the shelves. A basket on a hook. And on a stone ledge, wrapped in oilcloth, a field journal older than any in the family.
cache.ending: It's the founder's. It begins the winter they came over the hills with a basket and nothing else, and built a house in the hollow beside the Yew. Page after page of mushrooms in a careful hand: where they grew, when, and what they were mistaken for. Every name in it is one the family still uses. The last page is for whoever found it: "I hid our things all over the valley, so whoever came after me would have to walk all of it. If you are reading this, you know these woods the way I did. The homestead is yours. It always was." You carry the journal home and shelve it beside your own.
